chunks: We reply that he has only complicated his argument in this section, as logicians say, by turning around premises and referring them to one another,
and undoubtedly he intended to disguise lunacy beneath lucidity and fallacy beneath logic; otherwise, the subject is clearer than to be ambiguous.

When has the Imamiyah said that the administration of affairs by the Imam is not necessary during occultation, so it could be said your proof does not prove the necessity of existence of an Imam who is not administering the society, because this is the time of occultation?
On the contrary, what we have stated time and again is that his administration of society is necessary in all conditions – his occultation as well as his appearance.
However, during his appearance he is able to administer the society and he does that, and during occultation he is unable to perform that and does not do it,
because it does not remain obligatory anymore.
We explained that the duty-bound are to be blamed for this, as they prohibited him; they did not empower him, and took on the task themselves.
We compared this to the subject of faith in God time and again.

key_terms.انْبِسَاطُ الْيَدِ: Administration of affairs / Extending the hand

ai.seo_question: What is the Imami view on the Imam's authority during occultation?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi counters the logical complexities of his opponents by asserting that the Imam's authority (imbasat al-yad) remains obligatory in both the states of presence and occultation, with the difference lying merely in the physical ability to manifest rather than the cessation of the duty. He draws a parallel to human knowledge, arguing that just as knowledge persists despite being hidden, the Imam's divine authority remains fully active and incumbent upon the faithful even when concealed from public view.
